notes.title: Scalable NG+, Gameplay Modifiers and more
notes.notes:
[p]Hello, everyone!

This update introduces [b]two major features[/b], along with a few QoL improvements (including a couple that [b]have been requested for a while[/b]).

[/p][h3]SCALABLE NG+[/h3][p]The first big addition is [b]Scalable NG+[/b]: NG+ used to be a single mode with fixed higher difficulty, now features an [b]incremental scaling system[/b] (NG+, NG+2, NG+3, etc.). Enemy damage to the player, resistance to volunteers attacks, and the score multiplier [b]will all increase with each cycle, following a non-linear progression[/b]. [b]The number of available volunteers will now start at 5[/b] for NG+ and gradually [b]decrease[/b] [b]to only one volunteer[/b] from NG+5 onwards.

[/p][h3]GAMEPLAY MODIFIERS[/h3][p]The second major feature is [b]Gameplay Modifiers[/b]. From the main menu, you’ll be able to toggle a set of [b]optional features that can significantly alter the gameplay[/b] experience.
For now, there are five available:


[b]Realistic Reload[/b]: reloading with bullets left in the magazine will cause them to be lost
[b]Ammo Scarcity[/b]: ammo will be much more limited, requiring resource management, good aim and increased dependence on melee weapons.
[b]Random Starting Stats[/b]: each volunteer starts with buffs and debuffs to HP, max armor, melee damage, critical damage, and stamina, based on their height and age, plus a luck factor that affects critical hit chance
And two long-requested features:


[b]Full Equipment Recovery[/b]: if enabled, you’ll be able to recover all the items from a previously deceased volunteer body, instead of just part of it
[b]No Interactive Terminals[/b]: if enabled, interactive (command-line) terminals will be replaced with simpler, more accessible interfaces

[/p][h3]QOL[/h3][p]Finally, a few general improvements based on the feedback you've shared over the past few months and from various chats :)


[b]The Laser Rifle Light is no longer pitiful :)[/b] I personally liked it as a last-resort weapon, but now it should be more satisfying for everyone, with [b]improved damage output[/b] (8 -> 10) and [b]better energy efficiency[/b] (50% less energy consumption)
Certain levels that previously ended abruptly will now show a [b]countdown timer[/b], giving a brief moment to retrieve any equipment left behind. You won't have much time, but it should be enough to quickly reorganize your inventory
[b]Hidden rooms[/b] will now be, in most cases, less noticeable. You'll need to rely more on the [b]Detector[/b] to find them.

That's all for now.
Let me know what you think of the update, here or on Discord![/p]

notes.title: EMPTY SHELL 2 DEMO OUT NOW
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

A bit out of the blue, I'm thrilled to announce that [b]the demo for EMPTY SHELL 2 is now available on Steam[/b]!
Which also means that [b]the second chapter of EMPTY SHELL is well into development[/b]!

The game is a [b]direct sequel[/b] to the first chapter, and it comes with some major new features. Let me briefly tell you about the two most noticeable ones:

[list]
[*]As you can see from the trailer and screenshots, the K-Link satellite system used to monitor volunteers has received a major upgrade and [b]can now transmit color images[/b].
Not exactly the most colorful broadcast ever seen, I’ll admit. :)
[b]But for those of you who are fond of black and white, there’s an option to use the original K-Link view as well[/b].

[*] The second major change is the [b]gameplay loop[/b]: while progression in the first EMPTY SHELL was more traditional and linear, level after level, [b]in EMPTY SHELL 2, volunteers will be housed together in a building on the island, which they can return to even in the middle of a mission or with partially completed objectives[/b] (provided they find an extraction zone… and make it there alive).
They’ll bring back gear and resources to stash in the shelter, to be used later either by themselves or by future volunteers who will replace them in case of… unfortunate outcomes.
[/list]

Speaking of objectives, there will now also be [b]optional secondary objectives[/b] that can be completed at your discretion to top up the base pay promised at contract signing.

Alright, volunteers, I’ll leave the rest for you to discover: try the demo and let me know what you think!
As always, I’ll be here reading all your feedback and working hard in the coming weeks and beyond to fix everything I’m sure you’ll find that’s not working properly, unbalanced, or just off in any way.
[h3]One last VERY IMPORTANT thing: if you enjoy the demo of EMPTY SHELL 2, please remember to add the game to your wishlist and leave a review for the demo.
That’s the only way the game can gain enough visibility to keep development going.[/h3]

That said, load a couple shells into that old hunting shotgun and sharpen your trusty hatchet:
It’s time to go back into the Facility.

[b]MEDIUM[/b]
[list]
[*]higher probability to recover weapons/gadgets/consumables/ammo (10% more each)

[b]HARD[/b]

notes.title: Daily Test Rooms Out Now
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

[b]The Daily Test Room mode is now available[/b].
You will unlock it [b]after completing the main game, at any difficulty level[/b].
For those who missed the previous news, this is the summary of the new mode:

[i]You'll be thrown into confined spaces with a fixed loadout ([b]that will change daily[/b]) and a bunch of ammo, and you'll be fighting non-stop until your last bullet (though you'll probably die before reaching your last bullet).

There won't be pickups, but [b]enemies will drop health, armor, and ammo[/b]. A supply crate will be delivered from time to time as well.

[b]Some random player stats[/b] like stamina, rate of fire, max health, damage etc [b]will be buffed and debuffed[/b].

There will be a [b]leaderboard[/b] specifically for this mode, which [b]will be reset every day[/b].[/i]

In addition to this, the [b]difficulty will increase over time[/b], which means you will face enemies of higher tiers that inflict more and more damage. Similarly, [b]the player's damage output and score multiplier will also increase[/b].

It's time to run some tests, volunteers.

notes.title: (Mild) ammo rebalancing
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

This update brings a ammo rebalancing (mild, for now). You are more likely to notice it at higher difficulties, but in general:

- now there are [b]more Small caliber[/b] bullets and [b]slightly less Medium caliber[/b] bullets
- the spawn of [b]Shells[/b] and [b]Large caliber[/b] bullets has been [b]slightly reduced[/b] too
- the [b]prices and the amounts[/b] of bullets in the Upgrade Stations [b]have been adjusted[/b] (less cheap)

Also, [b]MD5A2-B has been buffed[/b], specifically:

- faster reload time (2.2s -> 1.5s)
- damage increased by 4%
- kickback increased by 48% (was too low due to the low rate of fire, compared to automatic weapons)

Misc:
- You will now see [b]how much bullets you're buying[/b] at the Upgrade Stations

notes.title: Ammo rebalancing
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

After some talks on Discord, i was thinking to rebalance ammo in the whole game, especially late levels.

The idea is [b]not to leave the volunteers without ammo, but rather to leave the volunteers with more fear of running out of ammo[/b] (it's something already there, but i'd like to emphasise it more).

I've seen a few screenshots (and i had a look once again at the config files) and i realized that [b]medium and large calibers are too abundant[/b], especially compared to small calibers.

This will scale with difficulty, so it will become more noticeable towards Nightmare/NG+ difficulties.

What do you think about it?

notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

I've just updated the Prologue to match some content (QoL updates, bug fixing, balancing and UI/effects options) of the full version.
This is just a technical update to prioritize the loading of the save files from the Prologue, rather than the Next Fest demo, that was only available in October for one week.

notes.title: COMPENDIUM + Iron Volunteer
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

With today's update, the [b]COMPENDIUM[/b] will be available in the main menu. It contains unlockable entries of the creatures that inhabit the Facility, with 3d models and extra informations.

Also, [b]Iron Volunteer[/b], a new game mode, is available upon beating New Game+. While similar to the latter, in this mode enemies will inflict [b]very high damage, but so do you[/b]. It is indeed a faster approach to the gameplay, with [b]little to no room for mistakes[/b]. Plus, [b]Devices will cost 50% less[/b], so it's a chance to try the ones you still miss.
Ah, you only have [b]one Volunteer[/b], then it's game over...

I didn't add a new achievement for beating Iron Volunteer, but you'll be rewarded with something else: [b]a crown icon will appear next to your name in the Leaderboard[/b], to prove that you have completed the ultimate challenge in the Facility.

Other minor changes:
[list]
[*]difficulty is now shown in the final stats at the end of the game
[*]Semi-heavy and Heavy Laser Rifles now deal quite more damage
[/list]

notes.title: Stats fixes
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

A couple of stats bug fixes, today:

[list]
[*][b]Kills, Deaths and Rounds Fired[/b] counters in the leaderboard were resetting after a "New game", now [b]they keep updating[/b]
[*][b]Equipment Found Bonus[/b] stat was increasing after opening the same box multiple times, now fixed to increase [b]only once per box[/b]
[/list]

notes.title: Some improvements
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

Here's the changelog for this update:

[list]
[*]Now [b]Upgrade Stations[/b] show the [b]type of ammo[/b] used by ranged weapons
[*][b]Beta[/b] and [b]Gamma Emitter[/b] Devices inflict [b]way more damage[/b] than before (and last a little longer)
[*]Devices prices has been tweaked (the mid-late game ones are [b]a little cheaper[/b])
[*]Fixed a problem with the [b]Found Documents[/b] that was preventing to get the [b]TRUTH[/b] achievement if you played the Prologue or the Next Fest Demo before
[*]Fixed a bug that was [b]misaligning some elements of the UI[/b] when changing the resolution from the pause menu
[/list]

notes.title: Worm difficulty scaling
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

Just a quick update for the Worm. Now [b]its wind-up time scales with difficulty[/b].
Still a narrow window between it lights up and the attack, but it's 75% larger on easy, 40% larger on medium and 15% larger on hard (didn't change on NIGHTMARE or NG+).

notes.title: Technical update
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone.

Just fixed a problem that could happen very rarely. Some player, after a crash on startup (even a power failure) had a config file corrupted that was preventing the game to boot properly.
Now it's fixed.
Also, one document (79) [b]seemed to spawn too infrequently[/b]. This is fixed as well.

notes.title: Small ammo drop + small QoL

Hey, everyone!

Another small update, today:

[list]
[*]Now Armed Soulless (except for the ones with Rocket Launcher) [b]drop a (very) few ammo on death[/b] (the amount scales with difficulty)
[*]I've removed the "floating" effect from the [b]Found documents screen[/b], to improve readability
[/list]

When close enough, the dropped ammo is automatically collected if you already own the same type of ammo or a compatible weapon (and have enough space in the inventory).
Otherwise is dropped in the form of a lootable package.

notes.title: Radios

Hey, everyone!

I've seen questions about the purpose of the radios being asked more than once.

They always had an [b]hidden[/b] purpose, but i decided to add another one (at least for [b]some[/b] of them).
This is also related to a [b]dark[/b] detail in a level on the East side of the island.

Let me know how it goes!

notes.title: Small update

[*] The price of the [b]Rocket Launcher Turret[/b] is now [b]850[/b] (it was 800) and the [b]ammo is now 3[/b] (it was 5): it was too overpowered after the Rockets/Grenades update

notes.title: Recoverable Stats
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

Thanks for all the feedback as usual. This update brings [b]upgraded stats as recoverable items[/b] from the volunteer dead body.
This should create a better feeling of progression and makes difficulty, while still challenging, less harsh.
You'll be able to recover [b]up to 3[/b] of your previously upgraded stats (if you had less, you'll find all of them).

[list]

[*] You'll always find at least one medikit and some ammo in the Upgrade Stations

[/list]

notes.title: Update: respawn after death and fairness
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

In this update i've tried to make less painfull (while still challenging) [b]respawning after death[/b].

While with the previous update i've increased the probability to recover equipment from the previous volunteer body, this time i've changed the spawn location of the body: they were spawning in the same room they died, but this means that, due to the layout diversification each time, could have been at the opposite side of the level (or straight in a boss room), that actually jeopardize the very purpose of recovering equipment.

Now you still have to explore and find the body, but it will be more [b]closer to the initial rooms[/b], rather than in some remote location.

[b]Obviously, I'm trying to keep the game very challenging... just more fair :)[/b]

Other than that, these are the other changes:

[list]
[*] The probability of finding equipment now scales with the difficulty level (higher on easy, lower on NIGHTMARE)
[*] Easy difficulty is now a little easier (less damage taken, more damage given)
[*] Nailguns are more powerful
[*] Devices prices have been tweaked (a little less expensive)
[/list]

Let me know how it goes!

notes.title: Recoverable items and more
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone!
This update brings some changes to the type and amount of items you can recover from a volunteer dead body. It used to be pretty much just credits (the probabilities of recovering something else were very low). Now [b]it's more likely to recover ammo, medikit (or plates) and sometimes a weapon or a gadget[/b].
The probability [b]scales with levels[/b], so you'll notice more starting from the third/fourth level.

[b]The amount of ammo you spawn with has been also increased a little[/b], always based on levels.
Also, [b]it's more likely to spawn with a "better" weapon in mid-later levels[/b].
[b]I've swapped a Big Soulless (the charging enemy) with another enemy at the beginning of the 8th level[/b], cause it was really out of place, especially if you had just respawned.

That's it for now!

notes.title: About recoverable equipment
notes.notes:
Hey!

i'm reading all your feedback (trying to keep up, actually!) here and on Discord and i was wondering if it would be better to [b]recover more equipment[/b] (rather than pretty much just a part of the credits) from the previously deceased volunteer body.

I remember we talked about this weeks ago but the general feeling was that would have made things maybe too easy, but now i'm puzzled.
[b]At the moment you have a very very little probability to recover some of the equipment, while you always recover part of the credits[/b] (from 5% to 35%, depending on the difficulty level).

What do you think?

notes.title: Starting bonus/malus
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! I'm testing some new [b]starting bonus/malus[/b] values for the volunteers.
Based on [b]age and height[/b], voluteers will have little starting bonus/malus for [b]health[/b] (and max health), [b]max armor[/b], [b]melee damage[/b] and [b]stamina amount[/b].

Essentially, the older the volunteer the lower the health (and max health) but the higher the max armor value (kind of due to more life experience).

Melee damage use a linear curve for the height (the taller the stronger) but is also affected by a custom curve for the age (where a volunteer in his/her late 20s/early 30s is stronger than younger and older volunteers).

[b]Stamina, on the other side, can only have a small bonus but not a malus[/b] (to respect the balancing in fights that has been tested for months).
In this case, the younger the better, BUT, shorther volunteers will have more stamina than taller volunteers (it's a mix of the two attributes, age and height).

[b]This values are not gonna change the gameplay dramatically[/b], but i think they'll give a little more personality to each volunteer: we are talking about, for example, a 12% range for health (so +-6%, i.e. [b]you could start from 94HP up to 106HP[/b]).

[b]Even if you catch the worst case scenario, things are still up to strategy and fight skills.[/b]

What do you think about it?

notes.title: Reloading
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

Considering the very positive reception of the idea on Discord, i'm implementing a [b]reload system[/b] for all the weapons.

It wasn't there from the beginning, deliberately, to give EMPTY SHELL more of a "Quake" vibe, but the game is shaping up in a way that a reload system would fit nicely.

Some weapons (most of them) will work with [b]mags[/b], others (like the shotgun and the hunting rifle in the prologue, for example) will have [b]single round[/b] reload (with a finite number of maximum rounds in the internal magazine).

[b]Dodging, aiming, or melee strikes will interrupt the action[/b], so keep a distance when reloading.
Also, [b]reloading won't be automatic[/b] (shooting with an empty weapon with spare ammo won't reload), so keep an eye on the ammo counter!

notes.title: Devices, upgrades and meta progression
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!
Just wanted to share some updates regarding the [b]meta progression[/b] in the game.

These days i'm developing new [b]Devices[/b], the ones you can buy from the main menu and in between levels. A purchased device is permanent: you need to reach the target level to unlock it and then you need credits to buy it: after that, [b]you keep it forever[/b] (even if your volunteer die).

On the other hand, [b]Upgrades[/b], the ones you buy from Upgrades Stations, are different. You level up your volunteer, but when he/she dies, you lose the upgrades.

And that was it, until today: i decided to give to the next volunteer the possibility to recover [b]SOME[/b] upgrades from the previous volunteer dead body, and maybe some inventory items as well (rather than just credits).

I'd like to keep it the survival way so, for example, if you die with a full inventory and 4 upgrades (i.e. health+, armor+, stamina+ and rate of fire+), if you're lucky, you're gonna recover [b]a weapon, maybe some bullets, and armor+ (and credits, as always)[/b].

I'm probably gonna scale the amount of stuff you recover with the difficulty you are playing.

What do you think about this?

Cheers!

notes.title: A useful tool
notes.notes:
The facility has been abandoned for decades.
While some parts of it are still functional (or require a relatively simple restart of specific generators), some areas are [b]left out with no electricity[/b].

That's where the [b]flashlight drone[/b] comes in handy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43340117/49472e7a4348e8a3966b65411d8438b755892176.gif[/img]

notes.title: Testing the new Grenade Launcher and better explosions
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone!

[b]Explosions[/b] were a little too minimal, so, in the full game, they'll use fire and smoke rather than just a circular shape; and will have better physics too.
